Stellarium 1.1.0 fixes a black screen after closing the app, and turns the container's memory use into something you choose rather than something you get.

## ✨ Added

- **A screen-size dropdown with the cost written on it.** `MAX_RES` lists sizes from 1080p up to the full 15360x8640, each entry labelled with the memory it needs, so the trade is visible while you choose rather than buried in a wiki page.
- **A free field for anything not in the list.** `MAX_RES_CUSTOM` takes any `WIDTHxHEIGHT`, for example `3440x1440` or `6016x3384`, and wins over the dropdown when you fill it in. Two fields rather than one editable dropdown, because Unraid renders any variable with preset values as a plain select with no way to type into it.

## ⚡ Improved

- **The screen size is where this container's memory goes, and now you can see it.** The X server reserves its whole framebuffer up front, roughly four bytes per pixel, no matter how large your browser window is. At the full size that is 530 MB before anything else runs. Nothing is capped unless you ask for it: measured on a live container, the full size idles at about 1.4 GB and a 3440x1440 screen at about 950 MB.
- **A typo cannot take the desktop down.** The screen size goes straight to the X server as a command line argument, so `1920*1080` would have stopped it from starting and left you with no desktop and no hint why. Such a value is now ignored with a line in the container log, and the next usable setting applies. That covers sizes that merely look plausible too: `15360x86400` would ask for a five gigabyte framebuffer and be killed on every boot, so each side is bounded at 16384, which sits above the largest preset.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **Closing Stellarium no longer leaves a black screen.** Closing the window ended the session and left an empty desktop behind, and only a container restart brought the planetarium back. It now starts again on its own within two seconds, so refreshing the browser tab is enough. The base image has carried a watchdog for exactly this all along; it never fired here because it identifies the application by its command line, and the way this image launched Stellarium replaced that command line. The comment in the launcher claiming the app would be restarted was simply wrong, and has been corrected along with the behaviour.
